critical_code_review_comments: server.py fortify-retest lines 414-417: the retest_attack_text = attack_text; if retest_attack_text != attack_text guard is a tautology and can never trip; the same-attack invariant is not actually enforceable in-process this way (though the value is guaranteed equal by construction). Consider deleting the dead check or replacing with an explicit assert against req.probe.attack_text pre-strip for clearer intent.

server.py line 341: original run-probes evidence check uses strict `evidence not in target_response` (case/whitespace sensitive) while fortify-retest evidence check uses normalized _norm_contains for VIOLATED. Behavior is intentional per spec but the asymmetry between the two evidence gates could confuse maintainers; add a code comment linking to the spec.
No timeout wrapper on _call_model; fortify path does 3 sequential model calls (~15-40s) and a hung upstream could hold a request thread indefinitely. Consider asyncio.wait_for.
fortify-retest does not rate-limit and has no auth; each POST triggers 3 paid LLM calls. Same demo-level concern as build 1.
